incident-bot: ALERT 5387654322 — org=VoltEdge, sustained qps spike observed in us-west causing request queue depth >90% and 95th pct tail latency rising. Paging SRE oncall: @Ryan (pager duty).

Ryan (oncall): on it, joining graph now. what timeframe did this start?

Jess Ortega: started ~09:12 PDT, ramped quickly after a customer job. error rate for gen endpoints is ~4.7% (was 0.2%).

Ryan (oncall): okay. first priority: protect the platform while we diagnose. Ana, can we temporarily soften per-org rate limits for VoltEdge or add a traffic-shaping rule?

Ana Morales: recommended: apply an emergency per-org soft bump (allowlist) for critical endpoints so customer can finish current critical workflow, then throttle non-essential routes. Plan: +3x org RL for 20m with auto-revert; concurrently block bulk-batch endpoints for VoltEdge.

Mike O'Rourke: thumbs up to auto-revert. also propose disabling streaming chunking for that org (falls back to discrete responses) to reduce connection pressure.

Ryan (oncall): okay executing. will run the admin hotfix and post command output here. Support Liz please prepare an outbound note to VoltEdge explaining temporary rate adjustments and ask them to pause non-critical jobs.

Jess Ortega: runbook refs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/qos-rl-hotfix and https://redwood.internal/dashboards/voltedge-qps

Ryan (oncall): running admin command:

```
# emergency RL bump for VoltEdge
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/VoltEdge/rate_limits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"multiplier":3.0, "ttl_seconds":1200, "reason":"auto emergency bump during qps spike", "actor":"oncall/ryan"}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION_APPLIED: org=VoltEdge rate_limit_multiplier=3.0 ttl=1200s actor=oncall/ryan id=hotfix-5387654322

Ana Morales: also applying a feature toggle to disable /batch/generate for VoltEdge: `featureoff --org VoltEdge --feature batch_generate --ttl 1200`

incident-bot: FEATURE_TOGGLE_APPLIED: org=VoltEdge feature=batch_generate ttl=1200 actor=ana.m

Sachin Patel: I'm watching ingress queue length and token consumption. after changes queue depth dropped from 92% -> 35% within 60s. 95p latency back to baseline over 3m. error rate down to 0.6%. nice.

Liz Kim: support message drafted: "Hi VoltEdge — we observed a sudden spike impacting availability. We've temporarily increased your rate limit and disabled batch endpoints for 20 minutes to stabilize service. Please pause any large batch jobs and reach out to coordinate a controlled ramp-down. We will revert changes automatically or sooner if notified." Want me to send now?

Mike O'Rourke: send now and include support escalation contact + escalation playbook link. + :phone:

Liz Kim: sent — transcript id 0x8f3a. VoltEdge acknowledged, says they kicked off a big backfill job accidentally and will stop it.

Ryan (oncall): monitoring metrics. will keep this thread updated, and if stable at T+20m we'll let auto-revert succeed. handing to Ana for longer-term follow-up and RCA. Ana — please prepare a post-incident note and propose mitigation (per-customer circuit breaker + early backpressure in SDKs).

Ana Morales: ack. I'll take incident lead. starting timeline and will open tracking ticket. pinging @Jess to capture logs for the RCA.

Jess Ortega: pulling traces and sampling KV cache heatmaps now. attaching quick snapshot: `s3://redwood-incident-archive/5387654322/snapshot-1.json`

incident-bot: NOTE: hotfix auto-revert scheduled at +1200s.

Ryan (oncall): handing to next oncall in 30m — leaving monitoring. :white_check_mark:

Sachin Patel: quick retrospective idea: implement a per-org ingress budget check that rejects bulk patterns earlier (500-level -> 429) with clear retry-after. will add to backlog.

Ana Morales: agreed. adding to mitigation RFC. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
